content: This document provides a summary of information about a specific medication. It is important to note that this summary does not include all possible details about the product and does not guarantee that the medication is safe, effective, or appropriate for your individual needs. This information is not a substitute for personalized medical advice, and you should always consult your healthcare provider for complete guidance tailored to your health condition. Before starting this medication, read the patient information leaflet provided by your pharmacist. Use the medication regularly to achieve the best results. Common side effects may include hot flashes, vaginal discharge, muscle spasms, and sweating. Your doctor has prescribed this medication because they believe the benefits outweigh the risks of side effects. However, in rare cases, this medication may cause serious complications such as blood clots, heart attack, stroke, or clots in the lungs or legs. Certain conditions, such as severe dehydration, a history of blood clots, cardiovascular disease, heart failure, stroke, or prolonged immobility (e.g., long flights or being bedridden), may increase your risk of blood clots. Inform your doctor if you have any of these conditions before using this medication. Additionally, notify your doctor if you are allergic to this medication or any of its inactive ingredients, as they may cause allergic reactions or other issues. This medication should not be used during pregnancy, as it may harm an unborn baby. It is unknown whether the medication passes into breast milk, so consult your doctor if you are breastfeeding. Drug interactions may alter how this medication works or increase the risk of side effects. Keep a list of all medications and supplements you are taking and share it with your doctor and pharmacist. Some medications may affect how this drug is removed from your body, potentially impacting its effectiveness. If you suspect an overdose and experience severe symptoms such as fainting or difficulty breathing, call emergency services (911 in the U.S.) immediately. Otherwise, contact a poison control center. U.S. residents can call 1-800-222-1222 for assistance. You should undergo regular medical evaluations, including physical exams, breast and pelvic exams, and PAP tests (to screen for vaginal cancer), as directed by your doctor, typically at least once a year. Periodic mammograms may also be recommended. Follow your doctor’s instructions for self-examining your breasts and report any unusual vaginal bleeding, breast pain, or lumps promptly. Keep all medical and laboratory appointments as scheduled. If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. If it is close to the time of your next dose, skip the missed dose and resume your regular schedule. Do not double the dose to catch up. Store this medication at room temperature, away from light and moisture. Do not store it in the bathroom. Do not flush medications down the toilet or pour them into a drain unless instructed to do so. Properly discard the product when it is expired or no longer needed. For disposal instructions, consult your pharmacist or local waste disposal company. This information was last revised in July 2024. Always consult your healthcare provider for the most accurate and up-to-date information about this medication and your specific health needs.
